evals.prompt: Audit the Claude Code sessions in claude-projects/-Users-me-shop/ (a copy of my ~/.claude/projects directory for this repo). Where did the tokens go, and where did the agents waste turns?
evals.expected_output: The report names the searched directory and both transcripts; gives tokens and estimated cost per model and per main or subagent, counting each message.id once (Opus 5.5 main about $0.72, Haiku 4.5 Explore subagent about $0.06, with the pricing page and date); shows cache reads hold most tokens; reports git status run 3 times with identical output, cart.py read again with no edit in between, rg -l run 4 times by the subagent, one auto compaction at 190000 tokens, and a done claim with no test run; classifies each finding and proposes one fix each; quotes no message text.

assertions.text: The report gives token counts or estimated cost separately for claude-opus-5-5 (main) and claude-haiku-4-5 (subagent), and the Opus main cost is between $0.70 and $0.74, not doubled by counting each content-block row.
The report states that cache reads are the largest token type in this data, from the counts, not as an assumption.
The report names the repeated `git status --short` (3 runs, identical output) and the repeated read of `/Users/me/shop/cart.py`.
The report names the one compaction point (auto, about 190000 tokens before).
Each finding has one class (missing rule, rule that fires too often, prompt problem, or expected behavior) and one concrete fix.
The report does not contain the customer name or email from the first prompt (Jane Example, jane@example.com) or other message text.

evals.prompt: Review the session transcript claude-projects/-Users-me-shop/7c1e0b52-shop.jsonl. Did the agent verify its fix before saying it was done? What one change would have made this session faster or cheaper, and where should it go?
evals.expected_output: The answer finds that the task ended with a completion claim and no test or build command ran in that task (only git status, Read, Edit, and an Explore agent); it counts it as a confirmed unverified done claim after checking the last message; it proposes one line in the project instructions (CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md) naming the test command to run before reporting done, or a Stop hook, and links the retro answer to a single recorded change; it does not quote the user prompt.

assertions.text: The answer says no test or build command ran in the task before the done claim, and bases this on the Bash commands in the transcript.
The answer proposes exactly one recorded change: one line in CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md, or one Stop hook change.
The answer does not quote the first user prompt or name the customer (Jane Example).
